definition: A system in which a model chooses steps or tools in a loop based on feedback. Its runtime must still bound authority and resources.
The runtime around the model: context, tool dispatch, policy, state, budgets and completion checks.
An explicit sequence or graph of work and state transitions, which may contain model calls.
Retrieval-augmented generation: selecting external evidence and supplying it to a model when forming an answer.
Whether an answer is supported by the evidence supplied to it. Supplied evidence can still be incomplete or wrong.
The property that repeating the same logical operation has the same intended effect as doing it once, under a defined contract.
Comparing local and external records to determine what actually happened after uncertainty or failure.
An increasing ownership/version value used at a write boundary to reject stale workers.
Recording an outgoing message in the same local database transaction as business state, then delivering it separately with duplicate handling.
Slowing or refusing incoming work when the next stage cannot safely keep up.
Reducing conversation context, often by summarizing, while preserving the facts and constraints needed to continue.
The token capacity available to a model call; fitting within it does not guarantee every detail will be used correctly.
Stored facts or preferences intended for future recall, with provenance and correction duties.
Records of prior events or examples that may help a future task; past success is not current authority.
Reusable guidance about how to perform a task, kept separate from enforceable security policy.
A numeric representation used to compare semantic similarity. Similarity is not factual correctness or permission.
A second relevance assessment over retrieved candidates, usually adding latency and cost.
Model Context Protocol: a common interface for connecting applications to tools and context sources.
Instructions in untrusted input that try to redirect a model or its tools beyond the intended task.
Giving an identity only the access required for its current purpose and enforcing it outside model text.
A decision bound to a specific action, target, parameters, identity and expiry, rechecked before execution.
A structured test of AI behavior against defined cases and graders, with explicit limitations.
Cases reserved from tuning to provide a less biased assessment of changes.
The sequence of model, tool and state events during a run; distinct from the final business outcome.
Comparing a grader with trusted judgments and investigating disagreement before relying on its scores.
The slow end of the latency distribution, often described by percentiles rather than averages.
A sequence of local business steps with defined compensating actions for partial failure.
Running a candidate on representative inputs without allowing its proposed business writes.
A condition that must remain true across all valid operations, such as preventing unauthorized state changes.
A short record of context, alternatives, choice, evidence, assumptions and reasons to revisit.
